title: No Travel Incomplete, Required for Safety (fallback: departure delay code 69, captain request for extraordinary security check), delay 6�9h, APPR, Basic Aeroplan
description:
Two-leg journey. Leg 1 operated on time. Leg 2 was delayed 7h 00m (inside the 6 to 9 hour band). There's no cancellation code and no arrival delay code, so the rules engine falls back to the first departure delay code, 69. The captain of AC 477 asked for an extraordinary security check at YYZ after an unattended bag was found in the cabin. The aircraft was deplaned and searched before it could safely depart (Safety). The customer was stranded at the mid-point (YYZ) and wasn't seen landing at YVR. Checks four things: (1) the MSL is Leg 2, (2) the fallback path is used, (3) code 69 is classed as Safety, and (4) NE-19 overrides the CAD 700 tier for 6 to 9 hours. It also checks that the Aeroplan Basic tier doesn't change the result.

Prerequisites:
PNR TC073: one adult passenger, Jacques Fortier. Two AC domestic legs, YUL?YYZ?YVR, June 1, 2026. Leg 1 AC 476 YUL?YYZ: operated on time, no delay codes. Leg 2 AC 477 YYZ?YVR: scheduled 12:00 ? 14:05 (local). Actual departure 19:00 (420 min late). Actual arrival 21:05 (420 min late). Status: DELAYED (operated). Cancellation code: NONE. Arrival delay code: NOT AVAILABLE (null/empty). First departure delay code 69 (FB), ingested as a DELAY_CODE event with state NEW. No other delay codes on the MSL. Customer stranded at YYZ, didn't board Leg 2, Leg 2 coupon not flown, no landing at YVR recorded. No Travel status: Incomplete. No rebooking accepted. Aeroplan: linked, tier code A (Aeroplan Basic). No expense receipts. Fallback: TRUE. Regime: APPR. More than 72 hours have passed. Filed within 366 days.
